reading.body:
CyrusOne's Council Bluffs campus publishes 9 MW of IT capacity, which at AI training density works out to roughly 225 racks and under 100 accelerators, a regional facility rather than a hyperscale AI cluster.

Disclosed power is the exception in Iowa, not the rule. The state has 52 mapped data center sites, and only two publish capacity figures, which together total 18 MW. OCB1 accounts for half of that. Any estimate of Iowa's data center load built from published numbers therefore describes a small fraction of the built footprint, and the undisclosed remainder is unknown.

The certifications describe a facility built for regulated enterprise workloads: payment systems, healthcare data, federal systems, healthcare compliance, and a data center infrastructure standard. That mix fits colocation tenants that need compliance rather than density. The 420,000 square feet of technical space against 9 MW implies a low power density, well below what accelerator racks draw.

What the data does not cover is who occupies the campus, whether it will expand, and how much power it actually draws. The suitability score of 56 is computed from published IT capacity and operator type, and it is flagged as missing announced expansion. The record also carries no coordinates, so it says nothing about proximity to substations or transmission. Published capacity is a contracted figure, not a measurement of load.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
